blocks.text: A danfo bus is licensed to carry at most 18 passengers. A JAMB pass mark is at least 180. Real life is full of limits rather than exact values, and inequalities are the mathematics of limits.

blocks.markdown:
An **inequality** compares two expressions that are not necessarily equal. There are four symbols:

- $x > 3$ — $x$ is greater than 3
- $x < 3$ — $x$ is less than 3
- $x \ge 3$ — $x$ is greater than **or equal to** 3
- $x \le 3$ — $x$ is less than **or equal to** 3

Unlike an equation, an inequality usually has infinitely many solutions, so the answer is a **range** rather than a single number.

### Solving is almost the same as for equations

You may add or subtract the same thing on both sides, and you may multiply or divide by a **positive** number, exactly as with an equation.

So $2x - 3 < 7$ becomes $2x < 10$, then $x < 5$.

blocks.title: The one rule that is different
blocks.text: When you multiply or divide both sides by a **negative** number, you must **reverse** the inequality sign. Start from the true statement $3 < 5$; multiply both sides by $-1$ and you get $-3$ and $-5$, and $-3 > -5$. The direction flipped, so the sign must flip too.

steps.text: Divide both sides by −3, and reverse the sign because −3 is negative.
Test a value to be sure. Try x = −4, which should work.
Test a value outside the range. Try x = 0.

items: An alternative that avoids the trap: move the variable to the side where its coefficient is positive. From $5 - 3x \ge 14$, add $3x$ and subtract 14 to get $-9 \ge 3x$, then $-3 \ge x$, which is the same as $x \le -3$.
Never divide an inequality by a variable — you cannot tell whether it is positive or negative.

blocks.markdown:
### Showing the answer on a number line

On a number line the convention is:

- An **open (unshaded) circle** for $<$ or $>$, because the end value is not included.
- A **closed (shaded) circle** for $\le$ or $\ge$, because the end value is included.

The arrow or shading then extends in the direction of the solution set.

blocks.caption: Reading inequalities in words is the fastest way to avoid mistakes

blocks.title: Translating exam wording
blocks.text: "At most" means $\le$, "at least" means $\ge$, "no more than" means $\le$ and "exceeds" means $>$. When a question asks for integer values, list them: the integers satisfying $-2 < x \le 3$ are $-1, 0, 1, 2, 3$, so there are five of them.

points: An inequality gives a range of values, not a single answer.
Adding, subtracting, and multiplying or dividing by a positive number leave the sign unchanged.
Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
Use an open circle for strict inequalities and a closed circle when the endpoint is included.
Always test one value inside and one outside your range as a check.
